title: Command ring and snapshot (O6): a wait-free path in and out of the engine, with loom models
zone: crates/octocore (ring, triple, snapshot, wire, attrs, link, sync, engine hooks, types), crates/octoffi (additive surface, octoffi.h, README), crates/octocore/loom, harness/baseline.txt (via cargo xtask baseline), handoffs/evidence
why_risk: adds a concurrency protocol to the audio path and an additive C ABI; an engine that never opens the link is unchanged, and tests E3 and the unchanged golden streams and determinism gate say so
spec_rev: SPEC-0001 r2 (owner approval 2026-09-29 15:11, O6 only); test plan specs/SPEC-0001/o6-test-plan.md
evidence: Every test was shown failing on a stub before the implementation: handoffs/evidence/o6-slice1-red.txt to o6-slice5-red.txt (slice 1: wire and attributes, 2: ring, 3: snapshot buffer, 4: engine link, 5: C interface). A few structural tests pass on the stubs by design and each red file says which.

The plan's 40 assertion IDs became 47 named tests, all in harness/baseline.txt (221 to 268 assertions), plus 2 ignored deep-soak tests that are run by hand. IDs: W1-W4, R1-R8, T1-T6 (T5 and T6 have two tests each), C1 (three tests) C2 C3 C4 C5 (two tests) C6 C7, E1-E4, F1 (two tests) F2-F6, the layout test new_command_variants_match_the_layout_in_the_c_header, S1 (two tests) S2 S3. The loom tests L1-L4 are extra and not in the baseline.

Loom (RUSTFLAGS="--cfg loom", preemption bound 3) passes L1 to L4. crates/octocore/loom/mutants.py breaks the code seven ways and the loom tests must fail each time (M1 to M7, all caught), and once in a way that changes nothing (M8, which survives on purpose): results in handoffs/evidence/o6-mutants.txt.

Soak in a release build, including the ignored deep runs (100,000,000 ring commands at two consumer speeds; 100,000,000 small and 2,000,000 real snapshots): handoffs/evidence/o6-soak-release.txt. No torn command or snapshot, no reordering, received + dropped == pushed.
Allocation: octoffi test e4 counts heap allocations on the calling thread across 1,000 rounds of push, render and claim through the C functions: 0.

Header: a real C compiler (cc -std=c11 -Wall -Werror) compiles octoffi.h with _Static_assert on 29 sizes, offsets and tag values taken from the Rust side (octoffi test f1_a_c_compiler_agrees...). Every line the header had at 9e4860b is still there (f4). OctoCommand is still 24 bytes.
Cost, measured not asserted, release build: publishing the 8,408-byte snapshot about 0.7 us per render; applying the full 256 commands about 7 us (handoffs/evidence/o6-cost.txt).

Gates: cargo xtask verify --base origin/metronome/queue-headroom: conformance, regressions, determinism pass; 268 assertions against a baseline of 268 after cargo xtask baseline. wasm-smoke passes locally: octoffi builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown and the three golden patterns match the native streams.
unresolved: The loom tests are not in a required gate: they need --cfg loom, so they are not in cargo test's list and not in harness/baseline.txt. Request to the Referee: journal/metronome/requests/2026-09-29-referee-loom-gate.md.
Snapshot LEDs and encoders are zero: there is no control map without panel.truth.json. The ring and buffer are ready for them.
ButtonDown, ButtonUp, EncoderTurn and LoadState are still no-ops.

ctx.playing on Engine::render overrides Command::Play and Stop from the ring (and from handle_command) at the start of core rendering. Who owns the transport is O4's question; recorded in tests/conformance/AMBIGUITIES.md.

An edit reaches the sound no sooner than the render after it is pushed, and a step less than MAX_EARLY_TICKS (12) from firing has already been decided. At 120 BPM that is about 31 ms; at 300 BPM about 12 ms. docs/02 section 6 budgets 1.3 ms for 'core apply, next tick'. Not a defect of the ring; a property of the lookahead that O4 will touch.

octocore_engine_handle_command and octocore_sender_push take Command by value from C, so a tag outside the enum is undefined behaviour in Rust. Swift's import of OctoCommandTag cannot build one; a validated raw entry point is the right fix and is not in this PR.

The direct FFI setters (octocore_track_set_i32 and the rest) still write the grid in place and are a data race if called while another thread renders. Documented in octoffi.h and lib.rs; the ring is the way to edit a running engine.
rustfmt: the tree already has 396 formatting diffs at the parent commit; this PR does not reformat.

title: Independent review of PR #11 and what was done about it
zone: crates/octocore (tests, docs, ring.rs reject, forbid(unsafe_code)), crates/octoffi (header test), handoffs/evidence, journal/metronome/requests
why_risk: as the implementation record: additive C ABI and a concurrency protocol on the audio path
evidence: Reviewer ran cargo test --workspace (257 passed, 2 ignored), the loom tests (4 passed in 28 s) and cargo xtask verify (268/268), and a debug-build fuzz of 2,300 seeds x 300 renders of random commands and raw words: no panic, no NoteOn with velocity 0, every NoteOn matched. Found no defect in the ring, the triple buffer, the wire format or the engine hooks

Finding 2 (C6 vacuous, CONFIRMED by deleting the push): fixed. C6 now renders with playing true and asserts the flush NoteOffs in the same render. Deleting the push fails it (cargo test -p octocore --test link c6)

Finding 3 (header test ignored enumerator order, CONFIRMED by swapping OCTO_CMD_STOP and OCTO_CMD_CONTINUE, and OCTO_TRACK_VELOCITY and LENGTH_FACTOR): fixed. The C compiler test now has a _Static_assert for every OCTO_TRACK_*, OCTO_STEP_* and OCTO_CMD_* value taken from Rust. Both swaps now fail it

Finding 4 (wire strictness only partly pinned, CONFIRMED by removing SetStep's stray-bit check and SetMode's range check): fixed with W5, which flips every one of 192 bits of every valid command and requires the result to be refused or to encode back to the same words. Both broken decoders now fail it

Finding 6 (cost measured only for the cheapest command, reproduced: 256 Reset commands 64 us median, 202 us p99): o6-cost.txt extended, source added at handoffs/evidence/o6-cost/bench.rs, plan and journal corrected
Finding 7 (red runs prove little): handoffs/evidence/o6-link-mutants.txt, 12 of 12 mutants of the engine hooks and setters caught (crates/octocore/loom/link_mutants.py)
Finding 9: MAX_ATTEMPTS and link stats docs corrected, Receiver::reject cannot wrap its counter, #![forbid(unsafe_code)] added to octocore, PR body zone list corrected
Verified after the fixes: cargo test --workspace 258 passed 0 failed 2 ignored; loom 4 passed; cargo xtask verify 269 assertions (baseline 269) conformance, regressions and determinism pass
unresolved: Finding 1: the AcqRel swaps in triple.rs (writer and reader) are not protected by any test. Loom does not model reordering past a later atomic operation and the soaks run on x86-64. The review broke each on purpose and nothing failed. Reasoned, not tested. Needs an aarch64 soak: request added to journal/metronome/requests/2026-09-29-referee-loom-gate.md item 6. Owner: referee. Also: the PR body's 'every interleaving' means every interleaving within loom's preemption bound of 3, on models of 2 to 4 operations

Finding 5: the snapshot leads the sound by about 13 ticks (measured 12.9). Documented in snapshot.rs and octoffi.h, Scribe request item 9. Not changed: publishing the audible tick instead is a design choice for the owner

Finding 8: the C header test is -fsyntax-only, so a function signature that disagrees between the header and the Rust definition would not be caught. A test that links C against the library is a follow-up. Owner: metronome
AGENTS.md crate table says octocore has no dependencies: request to Conductor in journal/metronome/requests/2026-09-29-agents-md-crate-table.md
